signals.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1: full-duplex voice API, $0.05/min, 12 voices
signals.summary: OpenAI's voice model now listens and speaks at the same time instead of taking turns, cutting interruptions ~80% versus cascaded turn-based systems. Live in the API today at $0.05/min with 12 voices and native transcripts, not a demo or waitlist.
signals.run_with_it_note: Wire GPT-Live-1 to one Twilio number this week for a single narrow job, e.g. an after-hours booking-FAQ line for one business, and see if a caller can complete a task without a human. This is the first voice model that actually holds a real phone conversation instead of a walkie-talkie exchange. Direct shot at the desk<->mobile gap: leverage that currently only exists behind a keyboard could start answering the phone while David is on a boat.

signals.title: Claude Fable 5.1 cracks a 370-year-old unsolved royal cipher
signals.summary: Fable 5.1 solved the Cyphral Distich, a 64-number cipher hidden in a 17th-century text that nobody had cracked in 370 years, by treating the numbers as word-indices into a companion document and pulling out a concealed royal prayer. Not clever cryptanalysis, just sustained attention on a pattern every human reader had skipped past. Hit #1 on HN front page today at 1070 points.
signals.run_with_it_note: No new build here, the underlying blog post is actually from Aug 31 (14 days old); it's the Spark because it just went viral on HN today, which is the real signal: sustained-attention pattern-finding on messy source material is now good enough to outperform historical human experts. Worth deliberately handing Fable a genuinely messy, unstructured pile of business data (old contracts, years of guest reviews, a dead vendor's paperwork) this week and see what it notices that nobody read closely enough to catch.

signals.title: LangChain's Paid Media Agent: an ad-ops analyst that proposes changes in Slack, humans approve, then it executes
signals.summary: LangChain built an agent that combines ad-platform data with pipeline data, generates weekly recommendations, and posts them as approval cards in Slack for a human to review/edit before anything touches the live ad account. Treated the agent 'like a new paid-media analyst': its own sandbox, pre-loaded tools, and company docs organized into skills/wikis it looks up on demand rather than one giant prompt.
signals.run_with_it_note: This is exactly the shape of David's own approval-gate pattern (kid-coach, chief-of-staff) and exactly the shape /google-ads already runs for Google spend, but Meta ads is still research-only (/ad-research) with no closed optimization loop. Cheap first test: take the LangChain 'skills + wiki + approval card' workspace pattern and sketch it as the missing piece for a /meta-ads closed loop, propose-in-Slack, David taps approve, agent executes.

signals.title: "How to Build an AI Software Factory": agents that open, review, and merge their own PRs
signals.summary: Firecrawl's writeup on running a pipeline of agents that open pull requests, review each other's work, and merge without a human in the loop for low-risk changes. Real pattern, not vaporware, HN gave it modest but real traction (31 pts, 13 comments).
signals.run_with_it_note: Not a Spark only because fit is generic (any coder could use it) versus the Paid Media Agent, which maps onto a gap David already has open. Worth a look if Sentry Tower's rebuild pipeline ever needs to scale past what one approval loop can review.

signals.title: Cognition's SWE-2: strong coding benchmarks at a fraction of the cost
signals.summary: New coding model from Cognition (Devin's maker) claims to push the cost/quality Pareto frontier for autonomous coding tasks. Single-source this week.

signals.title: OpenAI's Agents API goes public beta: managed infra for long-running, persistent agents
signals.summary: Removes the need to hand-build orchestration/state management for agents that run for a long time and call tools across sessions. Rented infra, not owned.

signals.title: Slack Surfaces: live, auto-updating dashboards embedded directly in conversations
signals.summary: Slack's new primitive for teams to build live reports/dashboards that update inline in a channel instead of linking out to a separate tool.
signals.run_with_it_note: Directly relevant to #the-helm's task-per-message loop, could eventually replace a wall of text status updates with a live tile. Not rolled out widely enough yet to test.

signals.title: GPT-6 Astra so in-demand OpenAI paused Pro plan signups
signals.summary: Update on last week's Astra launch: demand for the model is high enough that OpenAI froze new Pro subscriptions to manage load, first-cybersecurity-threshold model is now the thing straining their own capacity.

signals.title: Bluecore Energy: $50M seed for floating-barge nuclear microreactors, 2 months after launch
signals.summary: Oversubscribed $50M seed, just 2 months after a $10M pre-seed, for small nuclear reactors on floating barges powering ports. Not buildable by David, own_the_ground hard filter fails, but a second data point corroborating last week's 'return of the atoms' signal (YC S26 industrial/hardware share tripling).

signals.title: Meta previews Shared Agents for Muse, aimed at small-business support/sales workflows
signals.summary: Meta will announce shareable, customizable agents inside its Muse app for small-business customer support and sales at Meta Connect. Pre-announcement, not shipped, and entirely on Meta's rented platform.
